content:
incident-bot  [root]  Incident follow-up: small traffic spike in us-east (~11:40–12:05) on Hosted API. Breakers + load shedding were enabled for 2 models in canary. No Sev declared. Tracking here for notes + next steps.

Rafael Mendes  Confirming: this would’ve cascaded pre-breakers. We saw elevated inbound RPS, but control plane stayed responsive and GPU pools didn’t spiral. :thumbsup:

Christine Wong  Quick numbers from Grafana (canary only):
- Peak: ~1.7x baseline RPS for `chat.completions` (model `redwood-llama-70b`) in us-east
- Breaker opened for `(redwood-llama-70b, us-east, hosted-standard)` at 11:46, stayed open ~4m, half-opened, then closed
- Shed rate peaked at 9.8% for ~2m (mostly at gateway admission)
- p99 latency (successful reqs) stayed < 1.9s; previously we’d see 6–12s tail + timeouts
- Errors: 429 w/ `Retry-After: 2` dominated; some 503 w/ `overload_upstream_unavailable` during the first minute

Tomáš Novák  The big win: no queue blow-up in runtime. Queue depth capped and we didn’t see the “sawtooth then cliff” pattern. :pray:

Amara Diallo  Gateway side looked clean. Admission control was triggered by the routing hint + local queue depth. All responses had the new payload shape.

Amara Diallo  Sample from logs (sanitized):
```
status=429 code=OVERLOAD_SHED_EDGE reason=breaker_open retry_after=2 route=/v1/chat/completions model=redwood-llama-70b region=us-east tier=hosted-standard
```

Mina Haddad  Routing service: breaker state transitions matched expected hysteresis. No flapping.
We did see ~40s where capacity signal lagged behind (GPU util jumped, queue depth followed). Not bad, but worth tuning.

Ravi Menon  +1. The “lag window” is why we got a handful of 503s early. The breaker didn’t open until queue depth crossed threshold; by then a few requests had already been forwarded and timed out at runtime.
Proposal: add a pre-open fast path on “GPU saturation + rising queue slope” (not just absolute).

Sergio Costa  Dashboard snapshots:
- Breaker panel: https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/overload/breakers?var-region=us-east (time range already set)
- 429/503 by code: https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/overload/errors?var-route=chat.completions
You can see the exact open/half-open window at ~11:46.

Allison Grant  Metric labels looked bounded (no cardinality explosions). :thumbsup: The shed reason codes were consistent across gateway->routing.
One note: we’re missing traces for “shed at edge” decisions for ~15% of the 429s (sampling config?)

Christine Wong  Re traces: looks like the gateway path is sampling at 0.1 by default but the shed decisions should be forced-sampled. I’ll file a follow-up for Caleb/Logan.

Noah Patel  Runtime view:
- KV-cache pressure stayed < 65% in the window
- Prefill queue never exceeded 128 (cap is 256 in canary)
- Decode scheduling stable; no “back-to-back evictions”
We did not trigger the memory-pressure shed guardrail.

Rafael Mendes  This is exactly the behavior we want: shed early, keep the data plane healthy, keep control plane up. For customers, a burst of 429s with clear Retry-After is *much* better than random 5xx + timeouts.

Nikhil Sharma  Any customer tickets from this window? Just want to make sure the 429 behavior didn’t surprise anyone.

Tomáš Novák  Checked #support escalations + JIRA queue: nothing new so far. We should still monitor SUP intake tomorrow (some customers only notice after the fact).

Connor O'Brien  Release note: no action needed, this was canary config only. But we should capture this as “canary success signal” for the rollout checklist.

Mina Haddad  Action items I’m hearing:
1) Reduce early 503s by opening breaker earlier (slope-based / util-based)
2) Ensure edge-shed traces are forced-sampled
3) Evaluate if `Retry-After` should be 1s vs 2s for this class of spike

Christine Wong  On (3): during the event, recovery time to close was ~4 minutes. `Retry-After: 2` seems fine, but we could add jitter guidance in SDK docs (ensure clients don’t synchronize). We already saw the “herd” effect once in staging.

Amara Diallo  One thing: a small set of requests got 503 with `code=OVERLOAD_UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT` but no `Retry-After`. That’s a bug in the error mapping path when upstream timeout happens before admission decision. I can patch.

Allison Grant  Please do. Even for 503 we should include `Retry-After` when the system is in overload-protection mode, otherwise clients treat it like an internal failure and hammer.

Rafael Mendes  +1. Let’s treat missing `Retry-After` as correctness bug.

Sergio Costa  Also: alerting behaved well. No pages fired because the 429s are tagged as overload-protected. We got a low-priority notification in #eng-sre from the “shed_rate > 5% for 2m” warning (as intended).

Tomáš Novák  Nice. That’s aligned with the updated policy: load shedding isn’t an incident by itself, unless control plane errors or unexpected 5xx exceed budget.

Noah Patel  FYI: we should consider whether streaming requests should be shed slightly differently. This spike was mostly non-streaming. Streaming disconnects are a separate UX papercut.

Mina Haddad  Agreed, but for this follow-up: looks like success.

Rafael Mendes  Next steps / owners:
- Amara: fix missing Retry-After on 503 timeout mapping (please link PR)
- Ravi + Christine: propose slope-based pre-open input; share threshold suggestion in eng-sre
- Allison: work with Logan/Caleb on forced-sampled traces for shed decisions
- Sergio: add an annotation template to the dashboard for breaker open/close events so it’s obvious on screenshots

Christine Wong  I’ll create a Linear follow-up (under ENG-4821 umbrella). Also attaching a short writeup for exec update: “breakers prevented cascade during 1.7x spike; 10% shed peak; p99 held <2s; no paging.”

Connor O'Brien  Please drop the links here when tickets are created so we can keep the rollout tracker tidy.

Amara Diallo  Ack. I’ll open PR today; should be tiny.

Nikhil Sharma  Thanks all. If no customer noise comes in, this is a great data point for expanding canary to the second region.

Rafael Mendes  Closing the loop: if anyone sees delayed tickets referencing “sudden 429s” around 11:45–12:00 us-east, route to me + Nikhil. Otherwise, good win.

incident-bot  Thread marked as follow-up. If you create issues, please include tag: `overload-protection-canary`.
